claims.text: High configurational entropy promotes formation of a three-dimensional hierarchical twin-dislocation network.
A three-dimensional hierarchical twin network forms dynamically during rapid deformation.
The hierarchical twin network hinders dislocation motion and thereby increases strain hardening and strength.
Intersecting twin boundaries provide alternate pathways for dislocation motion and transfer, promoting homogeneous deformation and ductility.
CrCoNi is a single-phase face-centered-cubic alloy.
CrCoNi is an example of a high-configurational-entropy alloy.
The controlled comparison should use a conventional single-phase alloy with similar average elemental composition but lower configurational entropy.
Both alloys should undergo otherwise identical uniaxial dynamic tests over a series of strain rates.
Sample preparation and grain size should be matched, with a proposed grain-size range of 5–50 micrometers.
High-strain-rate loading facilitates strain-induced nanotwinning in the high-entropy alloy.
Relative to the conventional baseline, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate during dynamic loading.
Relative to the conventional baseline, the high-entropy alloy will maintain or improve ductility during dynamic loading.
The high-entropy alloy will contain a denser and more interconnected twin network than the conventional baseline after dynamic deformation.
The mechanism should apply at ambient temperatures and strain rates that activate dynamic plasticity in face-centered-cubic materials.
At extreme temperatures, mechanisms such as dynamic strain aging may dominate and invalidate the proposed mechanism.
The quantitative contribution of twinning may depend on temperature and stacking-fault energy and may compete with dislocation clustering or dynamic strain aging.
Failure to observe both a statistically significant mechanical advantage and a denser or more interconnected twin network is proposed as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant increase in ductility; unchanged ductility could therefore both satisfy the prediction and trigger falsification.
